partnershipPlan: Two parent partners review the completeness definition and the plain-language summary; a respiratory educator and a community hospital emergency physician review the outcome definitions before linkage.
socialListening: No social media listening; the family advisory council's notes on discharge teaching from the last year are read for themes about action plans.

items.theme: The yellow zone in a hurry
items.quote: Composite paraphrase: They went through the plan while we were packing up, and by the time we got home I could not remember how many puffs to give.
items.implication: Record whether the yellow-zone section was completed with legible doses and treat illegible doses as missing.

items.theme: A plan in the wrong language
items.quote: Composite paraphrase: The paper was all in English; my son read it to me, but he is nine.
items.implication: Record language preference and interpreter use and report the association by language group.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: Half the children I see at our community emergency were discharged from the children's hospital a few weeks before, and they never find out.
items.implication: Count revisits at every provincial hospital through linkage.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: My mum works nights, so the plan is really for me, and nobody explained it to me.
items.implication: Note whether the plan was explained to the young person as well as the caregiver for children aged 12 and over.

summary: Four composite voices on hurried teaching, language, invisible revisits and teenagers who manage their own asthma.
